skill.name: zlibrary-to-notebooklm
skill.description: Automates moving authorized Z-Library books into Google NotebookLM by downloading PDF or EPUB sources, converting EPUB content, creating notebooks, and uploading files.
skill.summary: Download authorized book sources, convert them when needed, and upload them to Google NotebookLM.
skill.author: zstmfhy

security_audit.summary: Most documentation URL, Markdown backtick, entropy, and troubleshooting command flags are false positives from examples or multilingual documentation. Confirmed issues remain around sensitive session storage, unsafe /tmp guidance, and shell=True subprocess commands that interpolate filenames, titles, and CLI output. I also found business logic abuse risk because the primary workflow automates Z-Library downloads into NotebookLM despite legal-use disclaimers.

remediation.issue: scripts/upload.py builds shell commands with shell=True using filenames, titles, and IDs.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True strings with subprocess.run argument arrays, validate notebook IDs, and sanitize generated notebook titles before CLI calls.

remediation.issue: The workflow references /tmp for executable helper paths and converted document outputs.
remediation.suggestion: Use repository-local scripts only, and store converted files in a private cache or temporary directory with owner-only permissions.

remediation.issue: Browser session state and optional credentials persist under ~/.zlibrary.
remediation.suggestion: Document consent clearly, avoid storing plaintext passwords, use strict permissions, and prefer an OS keychain for secrets.

remediation.issue: The primary workflow can facilitate unauthorized book downloads from Z-Library.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user attestation of lawful access and refuse requests involving commercial copyrighted works without authorization.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Command Injection Through Downloaded Metadata
semantic_findings.description: Downloaded filenames and derived titles flow into shell=True command strings for conversion and NotebookLM CLI calls. A malicious source can use quotes or shell metacharacters in filenames or titles to run local commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly constructs shell command strings with values derived from downloaded file paths and inferred titles. The use of shell=True makes metacharacter injection a concrete local command execution risk.

semantic_findings.title: Business Logic Enables Unauthorized Book Acquisition
semantic_findings.description: The primary workflow triggers on Z-Library book links, automates download, and uploads the result to NotebookLM. Legal-use disclaimers exist, but the workflow can still facilitate unauthorized acquisition or redistribution of copyrighted books.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly targets Z-Library links and automates downloading before upload. The disclaimer reduces intent certainty, but the enabled workflow remains a clear abuse risk.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Authentication State Stored Locally
semantic_findings.description: The login flow saves browser storage state and persistent profile data under a hidden home directory, and upload.py can load local Z-Library credentials. These long-lived authentication artifacts need strict permissions and user consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code and documentation show persistent browser session storage and credential loading. Permissions are partially restricted, but the artifacts remain sensitive local authentication material.

content.value_statement: Moving legally sourced books into NotebookLM can require manual downloading, conversion, chunking, and upload work. This skill automates that workflow for Z-Library-style links with login reuse, format conversion, and notebook creation.
actual_capabilities: Uses Playwright to open a Z-Library page with a saved browser session.
Downloads PDF when available and falls back to EPUB.
Converts EPUB files to Markdown using ebooklib and BeautifulSoup.
Splits large Markdown files before upload.
Creates NotebookLM notebooks and uploads files through the NotebookLM CLI.
Returns notebook and source IDs after a successful upload.
limitations: Requires Playwright, Chromium, ebooklib, and a NotebookLM CLI installation.
Requires a valid Z-Library session saved on the local machine.
Only supports content the user can lawfully access and upload.
May fail when source site pages or NotebookLM CLI behavior changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Reading
use_cases.description: Move a legally accessed research book into NotebookLM for citation review and question answering.

use_cases.title: Create Study Notebooks
use_cases.description: Convert an authorized EPUB or PDF source into a NotebookLM notebook for study notes.

use_cases.title: Process Long Documents
use_cases.description: Split permitted long-form documents into smaller uploads when NotebookLM limits are reached.

prompt_templates.title: Upload One Authorized Book
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill with this Z-Library link: [URL]. Confirm legal access, download the best available format, and upload it to NotebookLM.

prompt_templates.title: Convert EPUB Before Upload
prompt_templates.prompt: Process this authorized EPUB link: [URL]. If only EPUB is available, convert it to Markdown before creating the NotebookLM notebook.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Login State
prompt_templates.prompt: Check why the saved Z-Library session is not working. Tell me which login step failed and what local file I should verify.

prompt_templates.title: Process Multiple Permitted Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: For these authorized links, process one at a time, wait between downloads, upload each source, and return the notebook IDs and failures.

output_examples.input: A user provides one authorized Z-Library book URL and asks for a NotebookLM notebook.
output: Reports the notebook ID and suggested questions.

output_examples.input: The downloaded EPUB is too large for reliable upload.
output_examples.output: The skill converts it to Markdown, splits it into chapter-based parts, uploads the parts, and reports how many succeeded.

output_examples.input: The saved browser session is missing.
output_examples.output: The skill asks the user to run the login flow, then repeats the download after the session file exists.

best_practices: Use only public domain, open license, owned, or otherwise authorized materials.
Run the login flow manually before the first automated download.
Review downloaded filenames and generated notebook titles before uploading.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to obtain or upload copyrighted books without permission.
Do not run commands from temporary directories or untrusted paths.
Do not process links from unknown sources without checking the domain and title.

faq.question: Does this skill include NotebookLM itself?
faq.answer: No. It calls an external NotebookLM CLI that must be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can it process local files?
faq.answer: The skill focuses on Z-Library page links. Local files are better uploaded directly with your NotebookLM tooling.

faq.question: What formats are supported?
faq.answer: It prefers PDF. It can convert EPUB to Markdown and split large Markdown outputs.

faq.question: Where does it store login state?
faq.answer: The scripts use a local hidden Z-Library directory for browser session state and profile data.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with any book link?
faq.answer: No. Use it only for content you are allowed to download and upload.

faq.question: What should I do when download fails?
faq.answer: Check the saved login session, source page availability, browser automation, and NotebookLM CLI authentication.
